evidence:
This assigned row is satisfied at the prompt/probe level described by quality-checks.md:143: when a criterion concerns interaction, the judge is told to perform the interaction. The frozen workbook Quality Checks!C35:D35 and Internal Quality Checks!C35:D35 agree on this requirement. The frozen task is a desktop transaction workspace, not an animation/timer/theme/mobile task: instruction.md:5 explicitly says no dashboard, theme switching or special phone layout. Thus absence of mobile resizing and theme toggling is not an omitted requested probe. Calendar vesting is evaluated by entered effective dates and a stored reference moment, not real-time waiting (functional/prompt.md:41-43; functional/judge.toml:596,623,632).

Every dimension crosses real interactive states. gates/render/judge.toml:23 requires incorrect-password refusal followed by correct-password sign-in. gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-25 and prompt.md:5-7 require UI requisition/offer creation and independent-context sign-in/readback, explicitly excluding API-only creation and still images. Each scored prompt repeats UI creation and fresh-context readback. functional/prompt.md:17 requires capture of successful UI requests before prescribed replays; :29-35 explicitly performs approval, both revisions and rescission through UI, recording each resulting state before the next action. :39 and :47 issue actual concurrent operations and reread persisted effects; :49 calls a real restart before reopening/signing in. Coordinated protocols B1-B6 require ordinary Finance prepare/commit, stale-state changes before commit, concurrent retries, later changes, and original-receipt replay. Corresponding functional/judge.toml:956,965,992,1001,1010,1019,1028,1037,1046,1055,1064,1073 demand resulting saved states, not a displayed button or first paint.

Recovery is explicitly exercised. polish/prompt.md:12 requires refusal/correction for revision and one interrupted rescission request followed by unchanged retry. :14 requires a stale coordinated commit and correction; it also forwards a real successful commit, awaits its real server response, suppresses delivery, then retries the same saved operation. polish/judge.toml:23,32,41,50 make those interactions the actual full-credit evidence. Interception cleanup is required; normal successful controls precede refusals. Visual/prompt.md:10 directs navigation across all six screens and harmless detail/form surfaces at a conventional desktop viewport; visual/judge.toml:24,39,54,69,84 grades those observed surfaces without adding animated/mobile/theme behavior.

Independent raw-evidence verification: local/batch-ui.cjs SHA256 899a7309c67b2ca5f951ced6ce65c8e8c63634f5e892cc0427b4d97fef109821 and local/batch-ui/results.json SHA256 c58daecb432c2bde6e4b005c42e85662c3a7b4810f1aa828f6ba69708656a6e5 match the current raw index. All 14 result-recorded source hashes match the frozen task/solution bytes. Script lines 24-54 actually click/sign in, select/edit terms, await preview and commit responses, observe stale refusal, correct the key, forward/abort one real successful commit response, retry that same saved operation and read stored results in an independent Auditor context. Results lines 21-37 record these observations successful. The stale-editor screenshot was viewed and matches its indexed SHA256 fa4dcc768730f3929ec25e32cef086f7bf28e1c52fdf95af0b800be932c3d2e4; it shows retained 1.23 bonus, 2.03 fair value and destinations alongside an actual stale-preview error, supplementing the action trace rather than replacing it.

local/mcp/results.json SHA256 bad8d80ee96bda6a46775d4dfcc508371b96c50e3106cd9f4e27ffee1a6e4cc3 matches the index; all 13 before/after source hashes match the frozen app. Lines 87-158 contain actual MCP action/result records for UI creation, fresh-context login/readback, response hold/release, overlapping POSTs and forwarding a real write before aborting delivery. The response-loss record reports forwarded=1, realStatus=200, browserObservedFailure=true and persistedDespiteLostResponse=true. local/legacy-ui/results.json SHA256 5987573723fa800cf685965c8e2e3608570f6b7c14e83b1853b096ad744f3316 also matches the index and its 13 source hashes match frozen bytes; lines 47-75 record retained revision input and interrupted-rescission retry. These are scripted product/tool observations, not configured judge grades. The index explicitly has no full configured judge run; this Pass establishes the row's required interaction instructions and relevant tool/product feasibility only, and does not establish workload, Oracle/model/portal score or task clearance.
counterexample: Attempted weak-app explanation: a convincing static workspace or HTTP200/no-op create response could fool first-paint review, but the required unique UI creation plus independent-context readback prevents that shortcut. Indexed local/gate-witness/results.json (SHA256 fd8410bc91102874ef98edfdbacf19f7853687956e076acc684d36c565d9ec75, verified) records the no_op_create variant returning200 while reqSaved/offerSaved/freshReq/freshOffer are false and basic_gate_observations_satisfied=false. A dead-approval variant does pass the intentionally narrow creation gate; it cannot supply the later required approval/revision/settlement observations. No configured score is inferred from this local witness. Conforming-alternative check: a desktop-only app with native date inputs, different labels/routes, semantic date formatting and explicit draft-refresh controls is permitted by instruction.md:5, functional/prompt.md:13, polish/judge.toml:23,32,41 and visual/prompt.md:10. It is not forced into a phone layout, optional theme toggle, impossible date entry or a specific animation timing threshold.
